Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Shashi Shekhar Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sita Ram Yadav
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Shashi Shekhar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and Sri Sita Ram Yadav, learned counsel for the informant.
2. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants in F.I.R./Case Crime No.28 of 2023, under Sections 323, 504, 506, 308 IPC, Police Station Tarwan, District Azamgarh, with a prayer to enlarge them on anticipatory bail.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged on12.02.2022 against applicants and according to the FIR,
applicant no.1 is the brother-in-law of the informant and he alongwith his brother and father made assault upon him through wooden sticks and due to the assault made by them, he sustained injuries.

4. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that entire allegation made against the applicants is totally false and baseless and even from perusal of the injury report of the injured, it appears that however he sustained four injuries but three injuries were found simple in nature and injury no.1 was kept under observation but after X-ray, no abnormality was detected and therefore, it appears Rituraj Mishra And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162076938/
1 that informant sustained simple injuries.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. He further submits that however apart from the present case, applicant no.3 is also having criminal history of four other cases but out of four cases, three cases were of matrimonial dispute and one case is however of Section 376 I.P.C., which is of the year of 2014, in which he is on bail.

6. He further submits that maximum punishment provided for all the alleged offences is seven years and during investigation applicants were not arrested and after service of notice under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. charge-sheet has been filed against them.

7. He further submits that applicants are having apprehension that if they will appear before the court concerned then they will send to jail and therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, applicants should be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of the trial.
8.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submit that applicants are the close relatives of the informant and applicant no.1 took huge amount of money from the informant and when informant demanded his money then applicants assaulted him.

They further submit that in the incident informant sustained as many as four injuries but both the counsel could not dispute the fact that all the injuries were found simple.
9.

Learned counsel for the informant further submits that as apart from the present case, applicant no.3 is also having criminal history of four other cases, therefore, applicants should not be released on anticipatory bail.
10. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, apart from the present case, applicant no.3 is having criminal history of four other cases, but number of cases arose due to matrimonial dispute except a case under Section 376 I.P.C.,
which is of the year of 2014, in which he is on bail and his criminal history has been explained in the instant anticipatory bail application.
12.
As far as merit of the case is concerned, from perusal of the medical report and X-ray of the informant, who is injured of the case, it appears that all the injuries were simple in nature.

13. Further, applicants and informant are close relatives and it appears, some dispute is pending between them with regard to the payment of the money.
14.
Further, during investigation without arrest charge-sheet has been filed against the applicants and maximum punishment provided for all the alleged offences is seven years.
15. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.

Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

19. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicants shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
